svg.title: Pragma communication server, MCP contract, runtime delivery and completion recovery
svg.desc: Detailed implementation diagram of assignment provisioning, eight MCP tools, A2A envelopes, result acceptance, artifacts and publications, participant-scoped delivery, persisted bounded recovery, database tables, and runner-independent boundaries.
svg.text: PRAGMA / CONTROL PLANE / IMPLEMENTED CONTRACT
Communication, without implicit completion
Typed messages • durable conversations • native session delivery • bounded protocol recovery
01 / EXECUTION AND TRUST BOUNDARIES
The control plane owns policy; the communication service owns durable messaging; adapters own native runner behavior.
POLICY / GO
Controller + invocation supervisor
Pins execution, step, visit, attempt and package.
Provisions the assigned conversation/identity.
Builds prompt, allowed outcomes and example.
Starts the package; supervises its session.
Consumes accepted result; applies routes.
PROTOCOL / GO
Communication service
Authenticated Streamable HTTP at /mcp.
Validates envelope + reserved data schemas.
Scopes membership, audience and authority.
Commits effects + messages + receipts.
Persists recovery state; sends corrections.
RUNNER / PI RPC OR ANOTHER NATIVE API
Runtime adapter → agent
Private profile, scoped MCP connection + skill.
Passes assignment to the native agent.
Delivers peer/controller messages to session.
Reports actual busy / idle transitions.
Agent performs work and submits its result.
EXECUTION → STEP → VISIT → ATTEMPT
Provision once; recover the same invocation
Deterministic participant identity is scoped to all four identifiers.
Provisioning persists identity/session before launch; replay retrieves it.
A recorded accepted result is returned without launching another worker.
Replacement attempts fence older credentials. No cross-execution peers.
AUTHORIZATION ≠ SANDBOXING
Credentials and host limitations
Bearer credential is supplied to the native MCP client, never the prompt.
Local listener requires loopback Host and rejects browser Origin headers.
Authenticated identity determines sender and human/controller authority.
Host execution still has the service user’s filesystem/network permissions.
02 / EIGHT TOOLS, ONE MESSAGE TRANSPORT
Thread membership is separate from process lifecycle. A conversation cannot launch an agent or complete an execution.
create_thread
Existing participants in this execution; creator becomes owner.
add_participant
Owner / human / controller; add known identity, not a process.
remove_participants
Remove memberships atomically; preserve conversation history.
list_participants
Discover IDs, assignments, kinds and active / removed state.
send_message
Address recipients or broadcast; apply typed control effects.
read_messages
History / unread + cursor; ack_through records delivery acknowledgment.
wait_for_message
Long-poll up to 30 s; empty timeout is normal; no model injection.
close_thread
Prevent further writes; retain history; does not complete workflow.
03 / WIRE CONTRACT AND CONTENT
A2A 0.3 content parts are reused. This is not the full A2A task protocol. Custom kinds remain possible.
OUTER ENVELOPE
send_message arguments
"operation_id": "unique-for-this-content",
"thread_id": "assigned-thread-id",
"recipients": ["controller-id"],
"payload": {
"kind": "step_result", "version": 1,
"parts": [{"kind": "data", "data": {
"outcome": "allowed-outcome",
"summary": "factual handoff"
EXACTLY ONE DATA PART; OPTIONAL TEXT PARTS
Reserved payload kinds
step_result → outcome, summary; optional publication_id,
artifacts (objects), evidence references, named data outputs.
publication → files: explicit execution-files-relative names.
input_request → prompt; optional options; human + controller.
input_response → request_id + authorized human answer.
runtime_status → state: busy | idle; emitted by adapter.
Ordinary message / progress: no terminal workflow effect.
Unknown application kinds cannot bypass reserved contracts.
Both advertised schema and server validation are required.
04 / RESULT ACCEPTANCE — TRANSACTIONAL SEQUENCE
The agent chooses a configured outcome. The server verifies the handoff; the workflow engine decides what runs next.
1 AUTHENTICATE + FENCE
Worker belongs to active execution / attempt; assigned control thread; controller in audience.
2 CHECK STRUCTURE
Raw tool envelope + typed data schema; reject string artifacts, missing fields and wrong types.
3 CHECK SEMANTICS
Configured outcome; nonempty summary; no prior result; no unresolved formal input request.
4 VERIFY REVISION + FILES
Current publication ID; unchanged published digests; collect applicable configured output files.
5 COMMIT TOGETHER
Persist result, message, idempotency receipt and activity in the same database transaction.
6 RETURN ACCEPTANCE
state: stored + effect.state: accepted + routing: pending. Stored alone is insufficient.
7 ADVANCE VIA ENGINE
Supervisor sees accepted result; drains output/receipt, stops process; engine applies configured route.
BOUNDARY
What acceptance never means
Not human approval. Not proof that claimed checks are true. Not completion of peers or a concurrent loop.
Not a permission grant. Not exactly-once workflow execution. Process exit, chat “done” and idle turns cannot substitute.
05 / DELIVERY INTO LIVE AGENT SESSIONS
Database rows carry content. Notifications only wake readers. Native runtime APIs make the content visible to a model.
ONE CURSOR PER DELIVERY LOOP
Read → handoff → acknowledge
Adapter long-polls visible messages after cursor.
Database NOTIFY or timeout triggers reread.
Own messages are skipped as incoming input.
Peer/controller content → native prompt/steer.
Advance cursor only after successful handoff.
Reconnect with retained cursor; deduplicate.
RUNNER-NEUTRAL OBSERVATIONS
Pi runtime lifecycle
Prompt dispatch → runtime_status: busy.
agent_settled → runtime_status: idle.
MCP sends are serialized; unique operation IDs.
Up to three unchanged-ID status attempts.
Persistent report failure ends session visibly.
Quiet stdout never establishes idle.
HUMAN INPUT AND CONCURRENCY
Peer / operator interaction
Concurrent agents exchange publications/findings.
Sequential steps receive accepted handoffs.
Formal question → input_request → human reply.
Configured human gate stays authoritative.
Native RPC input can queue or steer a live turn.
Stored messages cannot wake a stopped process.
06 / BOUNDED COMPLETION RECOVERY
Protocol repair is deterministic. It never writes product code, chooses an outcome or manufactures a successful result.
PRECISE TOOL ERROR + DURABLE REJECTION MARKER
A / Rejected terminal result
Return invalid_argument / invalid_outcome / revision or file error.
Invalid data is never disguised as temporary unavailability.
Supervisor checks recovery; controller addresses that worker.
Message includes safe reason, allowed outcomes + full example.
Agent corrects its handoff; do not redo finished implementation.
EXPLICIT RUNTIME OBSERVATION REQUIRED
B / Idle, incomplete invocation
After two idle minutes without an accepted result, remind.
Exempt a pending formal human request in the thread.
Exempt an incomplete peer that is busy / lifecycle unknown.
If every incomplete peer is idle, recovery can prompt them.
No idle-telemetry runner: rejection recovery still applies.
DEFAULTS: 2 REMINDERS • ≥30 s APART • IDLE TRIGGER: 2 min
Persisted, attempt-scoped recovery budget
Execution transaction lock serializes acceptance and recovery; one deterministic message ID per reminder counter.
Normal idle recovery requires the idle condition; busy work is not inferred complete or failed from silence.
Accepted result stops reminders. Repeated status calls do not reset allowance. Restart/replay retains counters and deadlines.
After the last response interval with an unresolved trigger: persist exhaustion, fence identity, stop session, fail invocation.
Existing workflow retry/block policy applies. No automatic product repair, success inference, or authority escalation.
CRITICAL DISTINCTION
Incoming delivery is not outgoing retry
Correct invalid content → new operation_id. Uncertain transport → identical payload + same operation_id.
The adapter does not resubmit a rejected result. The model must act on the tool error or controller correction.
07 / PERSISTED STATE AND OBSERVABLE EVIDENCE
PostgreSQL is authoritative; in-memory sockets, wait goroutines and adapter processes are replaceable.
FACTORY-OWNED DATABASE SCHEMA
Conversation and completion tables
comms_participants → invocation, work, session, result, active.
comms_threads / comms_members → scope, owner, cursor, closure.
comms_messages → sequence, sender, audience, A2A payload.
comms_receipts → participant + operation ID + fingerprint.
comms_requests → formal pending / answered human input.
comms_publications → exact retained file bytes + digests.
comms_completion → runtime state, idle clock, rejection,
reminder count/deadline, exhausted reason (migration 000005).
MONITOR / CLI STREAM / EXECUTION RECORD
Operator projections
Execution activity retains messages, receipts and process output.
Completion rejection and recovery exhaustion are explicit events.
Controller reminders appear as addressed conversation messages.
Operator can inspect status, logs, messages and human decisions.
API result acceptance is separate from engine routing progress.
Delivery acknowledgment ≠ read comprehension ≠ executed work.
File bytes/digests establish revision identity, not product quality.
Raw infrastructure diagnostics stay in controller logs.
08 / VERIFICATION AND OPERATING CONSTRAINTS
Regression tests use private databases, a local MCP server and fake Pi processes. They do not make paid model calls.
STRING ARTIFACTS → CLASSIFIED REJECTION → CORRECTED RESULT → ONE ACCEPTED HANDOFF
The original failure is an explicit regression case
Covered: exact malformed artifact array; strict envelope; required fields; idempotent acceptance; verified outputs.
Covered: persisted corrections; replay/concurrent-supervisor deduplication; restart-safe limits; busy/peer/human exemptions.
Covered: native incoming delivery, ordered lifecycle reports, steering, truncation bounds and visible provider failures.
Limits: models may still ignore messages; unknown peer lifecycle waits conservatively; host runner is not a sandbox.
Deployment: rebuild/install binary and restart the service. Source edits do not update an already running service.
09 / LIVE MESSAGE EXCHANGE — SEQUENCE TRACE
Solid arrows are requests/actions. Dashed arrows return content. Reads use retained cursors; all lanes share one execution scope.
Agent A
Adapter A
MCP / comms
PostgreSQL
Adapter B
Agent B
1 list_participants(thread_id)
IDs, responsibilities, active membership
2 send_message: publication(files)
Verify bytes; retain publication + message + receipt
publication_id + verified references
3 send_message to peer: revision + requested review
Append audience-scoped message; NOTIFY after commit
4 wait_for_message(after cursor)
Visible retained messages + next cursor
Native queued / steering prompt with exact message content
read_messages(ack_through): delivered, not executed
5 send_message: concrete review findings to Agent A
Adapter A reads findings using its independent cursor
Native input: findings + revision references
6 send_message: step_result(outcome, summary, publication_id)
Validate current revision / outputs; commit result + receipt
effect.state: accepted; routing: pending
Adapter observes its worker’s committed terminal message
Native session can finish; supervisor consumes persisted result
7 ALTERNATE: malformed result artifacts: ["file.md"]
invalid_argument: artifact objects expected; no completion
8 Native agent settles → runtime_status: idle
Persist rejection / lifecycle; supervisor checks recovery budget
Controller correction arrives through normal retained delivery
9 Wake session: precise repair + complete result example
Corrected handoff, new operation_id; no repeated product work
The control-plane supervisor is outside these native session lanes: it provisions them, consumes accepted results and applies configured routes.
Implementation: docs/communications.md • internal/comms • internal/commandrunner • adapters/pi
PRAGMA / TECHNICAL REFERENCE / 01 NOVEMBER 2026
